# Why is my dental software missing from AI answers?

A comparison question can leave most of the checked dental vendors out. In the 22 September 2026 captures, the Dentrix-versus-Eaglesoft question left 16 of 20 vendors unnamed across its 15 valid answers; across the full 149-answer dental panel, four checked vendors were never named. Those observations establish the gaps, without explaining why your software was omitted.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [September dental panel](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) used ten fixed questions and three runs on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode. Of 150 scheduled observations, 149 were valid; one Google AI Overviews observation returned no Overview. The table retains the vendors with zero naming observations across that valid collection.

| Checked vendor | Named answers |
| --- | --- |
| Dentally | 0 of 149 |
| DSN | 0 of 149 |
| MacPractice | 0 of 149 |
| XLDent | 0 of 149 |

For each zero-of-149 row, the descriptive 95 percent Wilson interval is 0.0 to 2.5 percent, a statistical range around the observed share. The event is a name matched in an answer under the published rule, not a test of clinical work, installation numbers or product availability. The data was published on 23 September 2026.

Question bases differ: the very-small-office question has 14 valid answers, while the Dentrix-versus-Eaglesoft comparison has 15. The observation without an Overview is excluded from the valid base, rather than counted as another vendor absence.

### The complete engine roster

This alphabetical roster retains every checked vendor and zero from the same 149 answers. Cells count named answers against each engine's stated base, not a new sample.

| Vendor | ChatGPT (base 30) | Claude (base 30) | Perplexity (base 30) | Google AI Overviews (base 29) | Google AI Mode (base 30) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ABELDent | 0 | 1 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| ACE Dental | 0 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Adit | 0 | 3 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| CareStack | 14 | 11 | 12 | 12 | 14 |
| Carestream Dental | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Curve Dental | 19 | 25 | 21 | 23 | 27 |
| Dentally | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| DentiMax | 0 | 6 | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| Dentrix | 22 | 26 | 21 | 24 | 27 |
| Dentrix Ascend | 21 | 22 | 15 | 18 | 21 |
| Dentrix Enterprise | 1 | 5 | 3 | 0 | 2 |
| DSN | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Eaglesoft | 14 | 18 | 12 | 12 | 13 |
| MacPractice | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Open Dental | 22 | 24 | 23 | 24 | 25 |
| Oryx Dental | 1 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 3 |
| Planet DDS (Denticon) | 12 | 12 | 11 | 4 | 9 |
| Practice-Web | 0 | 3 | 3 | 5 | 10 |
| tab32 | 5 | 14 | 13 | 5 | 2 |
| XLDent | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

These naming observations do not test UK clinical workflows, product reliability or compliance.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), ChatGPT responded to the new-practice dental software question on 22 September 2026, run 2, and described Curve Dental with the fragment “It includes scheduling, charting, imaging, and billing.” This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** AI search visibility work, often called GEO (generative engine optimization) or AEO (answer engine optimization), needs the practice setting. The published question set covers a new practice, a very small office and a dental service organization with several locations in separate questions; category-wide zeros do not replace them.

Keep brands, editions and aliases distinct; read the actual answer and separate later product changes from the dated observation.

Compare a disputed passage with a dated product source. medixdental.com appeared in 47 of 149 category source lists, but that pooled count does not explain a missing vendor. An [absence](../../named-zero-times.md) establishes neither a missing feature nor a reason to reject the product; a correction needs specific factual evidence.

### Dentally's reported UK product scope

**Reported.** Dentally's [UK partner page](https://www.dentally.com/en-gb/partners), read on 29 October 2026, describes cloud practice software and advertises National Health Service (NHS) integration in England, Wales and Scotland and Health and Social Care (HSC) integration in Northern Ireland. Its marketplace names imaging, communication, payment and reporting partners. These are published product statements, without a functionality test here.

The page distinguishes the platform from Xero's accounting connection and Dentally Imaging Bridge's connection to compatible imaging software. Setup varies by partner and may require enabling the integration in Dentally or completing partner setup. Check the region, submission operation, connection, plan and migration scope separately.

**Reasoned.** The [dental buyer questions](https://index.broadcastwell.com/questions/dental-practice-management/), including the [purchase-criteria question](https://index.broadcastwell.com/questions/dental-practice-management/what-should-i-look-for-in-dental-practice-management-software/), concern small offices, alternatives, product comparisons and purchase criteria. They do not form a UK-only practice sample. [Dentally's measured record](https://index.broadcastwell.com/vendors/dentally/dental-practice-management/) is an absence observation, not a verdict about UK clinical workflows, compliance, reliability, cloud suitability or whether advertised integrations work.

# Can an AI answer cite a company without naming it?

Yes. In [Volume II](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21586091), nine of 85 companies received at least one own-domain citation while their brands had no naming observations across their ten answers. Those answers were captured from July 18 to 23, 2026, under independent naming and citation rules. A cited publisher could therefore supply evidence without appearing as a product option. The September Index uses a different citation definition.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Volume II scoring method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21586091) recorded two independent binary events for each answer: the company's brand named and its own domain cited. The sample covered 85 selected B2B (business-to-business) software companies, ten questions each, with one run per question on one engine using live web search. Nine companies had zero naming observations and at least one own-domain citation.

This historical definition matters. The [September Index's scoring method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) instead requires the vendor to be named and its domain cited in the same answer. You cannot use the nine historical cases as if they were exceptions to that later event definition.

The July result does not establish why an engine used a source or which page change would make its publisher a candidate.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

**Reported.** Google’s [AI features guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 29 October 2026, requires a supporting page to be indexed and eligible for a Search snippet. It advises keeping Business Profile information current, without requiring a special AI file or new schema type. OpenAI’s [Search help](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), read that day, describes location-sensitive local results and says approximate IP-derived location can affect them; specifying a city, neighborhood or postal code can clarify the area. Its [crawler documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), also read that day, separates OAI-SearchBot search access from GPTBot training access. Host or content-delivery-network restrictions also affect access.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Inspect the cited page separately from the answer's proposed products. A page may supply evidence about a category, a workflow or another company. Its appearance among sources does not require the answer to describe its publisher as a vendor option.

The useful report keeps both fields and their definitions. If you receive a citation total from a different release or platform, first check whether naming is a prerequisite. Otherwise an apparent contradiction may be only a change in what is counted.

- **If you publish the source:** preserve the cited URL and the answer that used it. Do not label the event as a recommendation without reading the context.
- **If you report visibility:** for GEO (generative engine optimization), also called AEO (answer engine optimization) or AI search visibility, state the release and citation rule beside the number, especially when comparing historical data.
- **If you buy software:** separate the publishers of supporting material from the products the answer proposes for your need.

The same discipline applies when a domain supports several products. A domain match identifies a source relationship under a rule; it does not, by itself, establish which product claim was supported or whether that claim was sound.

A local service page illustrates that distinction: a vehicle-glass safety article can supply evidence without recommending its publisher as a nearby windshield operator. Keep the requested town and actual service area beside the answer, then inspect whether a citation points to the shop’s service page, another operator or general advice. These are reasoned checks, not measured auto-glass outcomes. See [valid measurement](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/valid-measurement/) for the separation between an observation and an intervention claim.

# Can an AI answer cite a company without naming it?

Yes. In [Volume II](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21586091), nine of 85 companies received at least one own-domain citation while their brands had no naming observations across their ten answers. Those answers were captured from July 18 to 23, 2026, under independent naming and citation rules. A cited publisher could therefore supply evidence without appearing as a product option. The September Index uses a different citation definition.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Volume II scoring method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21586091) recorded two independent binary events for each answer: the company's brand named and its own domain cited. The sample covered 85 selected B2B (business-to-business) software companies, ten questions each, with one run per question on one engine using live web search. Nine companies had zero naming observations and at least one own-domain citation.

This historical definition matters. The [September Index's scoring method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) instead requires the vendor to be named and its domain cited in the same answer. You cannot use the nine historical cases as if they were exceptions to that later event definition.

The July result does not establish why an engine used a source or which page change would make its publisher a candidate.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

**Reported.** Google’s [AI features guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 29 October 2026, requires a supporting page to be indexed and eligible for a Search snippet. It advises keeping Business Profile information current, without requiring a special AI file or new schema type. OpenAI’s [Search help](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), read that day, describes location-sensitive local results and says approximate IP-derived location can affect them; specifying a city, neighborhood or postal code can clarify the area. Its [crawler documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), also read that day, separates OAI-SearchBot search access from GPTBot training access. Host or content-delivery-network restrictions also affect access.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Inspect the cited page separately from the answer's proposed products. A page may supply evidence about a category, a workflow or another company. Its appearance among sources does not require the answer to describe its publisher as a vendor option.

The useful report keeps both fields and their definitions. If you receive a citation total from a different release or platform, first check whether naming is a prerequisite. Otherwise an apparent contradiction may be only a change in what is counted.

- **If you publish the source:** preserve the cited URL and the answer that used it. Do not label the event as a recommendation without reading the context.
- **If you report visibility:** for GEO (generative engine optimization), also called AEO (answer engine optimization) or AI search visibility, state the release and citation rule beside the number, especially when comparing historical data.
- **If you buy software:** separate the publishers of supporting material from the products the answer proposes for your need.

The same discipline applies when a domain supports several products. A domain match identifies a source relationship under a rule; it does not, by itself, establish which product claim was supported or whether that claim was sound.

A local service page illustrates that distinction: a vehicle-glass safety article can supply evidence without recommending its publisher as a nearby windshield operator. Keep the requested town and actual service area beside the answer, then inspect whether a citation points to the shop’s service page, another operator or general advice. These are reasoned checks, not measured auto-glass outcomes. See [valid measurement](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/valid-measurement/) for the separation between an observation and an intervention claim.

# How should I use robots.txt to control AI crawler access?

Broadcastwell's [robots.txt](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/robots.txt), served on 2 November 2026, has separate Googlebot and Google-Extended groups, each with `Allow: /`. Choose the group for the crawler and use you intend to control, then set the relevant path rule. Our file records a declared access policy; it does not establish a visit, crawler compliance, training use or an answer citation. The provider's documentation is needed to identify each crawler's purpose.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Agent Gap task method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23197560) recorded three public website tasks across 70 software vendors. It recorded 206 correct results, three incorrect and one unscored across 210 initial sessions. Thirty repeat sessions were separate. The study did not compare crawler policies, authenticate bot identities or test whether a rules change caused an answer to cite a page.

In the 6 October 2026 Agent Gap collection, all 210 initial tasks found a target page and 163 reached the defined endpoint.

**Reported.** Google's [AI feature guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read 28 October 2026, identifies Googlebot rules as the crawl control for Search, including its AI features. Google-Extended governs different uses, including training and grounding in other Google products. Google's [robots.txt introduction](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro), read the same date, explains that crawler instructions depend on crawler cooperation and do not secure private content.

### A separate description-task count

The [Agent Gap protocol](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23197560) records reached endpoints in 67 of 70 initial Describe tasks on 6 October 2026. Those tasks concerned vendors' public websites. They did not identify the requests as OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot or an Anthropic robot, or test the effect of a robots rule. This description-task cut is part of the broader task collection above; it must not be added to that collection's endpoint total. A reached endpoint is not a verified crawler visit.

### Provider purposes and the host being controlled

**Reported.** OpenAI's [bot documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), read on 29 October 2026, separates OAI-SearchBot for search from GPTBot for training. It describes ChatGPT-User as acting on user requests, separately from automatic search crawling. [Anthropic's crawler article](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/8896518-does-anthropic-crawl-data-from-the-web-and-how-can-site-owners-block-the-crawler), also read on 29 October 2026, distinguishes ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User and gives their purposes and robots.txt instructions.

Anthropic distinguishes Claude-User's user-directed retrieval from Claude-SearchBot's search purpose. Its guide places robots.txt controls on the site or subdomain concerned. A documentation subdomain therefore needs its own addressed rule record, rather than an assumption that the homepage's file controls that separate host.

OpenAI's [search help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), read on 29 October 2026, also asks publishers to allow traffic from its published searchbot IP (Internet Protocol) addresses at the host. A robots permission and a host restriction are separate checks; changing one does not verify the other. The bot's documented purpose, the declared policy and any actual observed visit remain distinct evidence.

**Reasoned.** If the intended policy restricts training while permitting search, inspect the separate named tokens. For an agency managing a documentation subdomain, record the intended purpose, exact bot and inspected address. A later answer that omits a company would need its own answer record; it would not identify which robot requested the page.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** First write the access decision in plain language. You may want a public source available to search while choosing a different policy for another use. An undifferentiated instruction to block AI cannot express those separate decisions reliably.

Identify the provider's documented crawler token and the exact paths affected. Review the existing rules before adding a new group; a broad rule may cover more public content than the page you had in mind. Test representative allowed and disallowed URLs against the intended rule interpretation, then inspect the actual served robots.txt file.

Keep hosting and access controls in the same review. A page permitted by robots.txt can still be unavailable because of its server or delivery settings. A disallow instruction is also different from a request to remove a URL from search results. Use the provider's documented indexing or snippet controls for that separate goal.

Preserve a dated before-and-after rule record and the reason for the change. Verification should show which published rule applies to which URL. It cannot certify that every crawler obeyed it, that an assistant completed a task or that a future answer will include your company.

See [the Manual’s citation chapter](../../who-gets-cited.md).

- **For a site owner:** separate search access from other provider uses.
- **For a developer:** test the named token and affected paths before changing the served file.
- **For an agency:** report policy delivery separately from observed requests or answers.

What do AI crawlers do, and how can site owners control access?

It describes ChatGPT-User as acting on user requests, separately from automatic search crawling. [Anthropic's crawler article](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/8896518-does-anthropic-crawl-data-from-the-web-and-how-can-site-owners-block-the-crawler), also read on 29 October 2026, distinguishes ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User and gives their purposes and robots.txt instructions.

Anthropic distinguishes Claude-User's user-directed retrieval from Claude-SearchBot's search purpose. Its guide places robots.txt controls on the site or subdomain concerned. A documentation subdomain therefore needs its own addressed rule record, rather than an assumption that the homepage's file controls that separate host.

OpenAI's [search help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), read on 29 October 2026, also asks publishers to allow traffic from its published searchbot IP (Internet Protocol) addresses at the host. A robots permission and a host restriction are separate checks; changing one does not verify the other. The bot's documented purpose, the declared policy and any actual observed visit remain distinct evidence.

**Reasoned.** If the intended policy restricts training while permitting search, inspect the separate named tokens. For an agency managing a documentation subdomain, record the intended purpose, exact bot and inspected address. A later answer that omits a company would need its own answer record; it would not identify which robot requested the page.
